payload.title: Grep scrub hides command substitutions that still execute before grep
payload.description: The new grep-family carrier treats the first quoted grep pattern as inert text and scrubs it before destructive-pattern checks. Double-quoted shell arguments are not inert: command substitutions are expanded by the shell before grep runs. A command such as `grep "$(rm -rf /tmp/victim)" file` or a backtick equivalent can have the `rm -rf` removed from `_cmd_match`, allowing the hook to return success while Bash executes the destructive substitution.
payload.recommendation: Do not scrub double-quoted grep arguments containing `$(`, backticks, arithmetic expansion, or other shell expansions. Prefer only single-quoted grep patterns as inert text, or parse with a shell-aware tokenizer and reject/surface any expandable quoted carrier.

payload.title: Once-bound mktemp variable proof misses shell assignment commands in control-flow heads
payload.description: The new `rm -rf` allowance trusts a variable if `_fr2_var_value` sees exactly one assignment to `$(mktemp -d)`, but its assignment counter only recognizes assignments at a limited set of separators. Shell assignment-only commands in positions like an `if` condition can rebind the variable without being counted or flagged by `_fr2_rebindable`. For example, `T=$(mktemp -d); if T=/; then rm -rf "$T"; fi` can be classified as deleting a trusted mktemp directory even though Bash reassigns `T` to `/` before the sink.
payload.recommendation: Treat any additional `NAME=` token in command position as a rebind, including after reserved words such as `if`, `while`, `until`, `then`, `do`, and after new compound-command boundaries. For this safety hook, the safer fix is to refuse variable-based allowances whenever the command contains shell control flow or compound commands.
